**ERAS** (Enhanced Recovery After Surgery) is an evidence-based, multimodal care pathway program that serves as the foundational knowledge base for clinical recommendations regarding early patient mobilization in Danish acute surgery [^src1]. Specifically, it informs the guidelines for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], a central quality metric that tracks the proportion of acute surgical patients mobilized within the first 24 postoperative hours [^src1]. 

In the context of the 2023–2024 Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) report, ERAS is highlighted as the evidence base justifying the push for early mobilization, particularly for acute high-risk patients [^src1]. The report discusses the ERAS program alongside the clinical risks associated with delayed mobilization, framing it within a broader narrative of systematic quality improvement and standardized, measurable indicators in the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
